mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which may lead to wage inflation and subsequently higher interest rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which may lead to negative economic growth and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is below 2% year-over-year, it indicates a potential monetary policy misalignment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month and UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month indicates weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strong supply-side expansion, which may lead to positive economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal.
